html:
The Tzeltal are a Maya people of the highlands of Chiapas, in southern Mexico. They speak Tzeltal, a Mayan language close to that of their neighbours the Tzotzil, and number more than half a million.

They are maize farmers, living in towns and hamlets on the slopes around San Cristóbal de las Casas and down into the forests to the east, toward the Lacandon. Their ancestors were part of the world of the Maya city-states.

Spanish conquerors took Chiapas in the 1520s. The friar Bartolomé de las Casas became its bishop in 1544 and argued for Native rights. In 1712 the Tzeltal of Cancuc led a great revolt against Spanish rule, which was crushed. In 1994 many Tzeltal joined the Zapatista uprising.
